take_homes: Giving the agent less access is a mitigation. Scope down before adding more.
The attack can be plain text in a doc the agent reads, so a good-looking output doesn't prove it's safe.
A skill is an easy way to hand a teammate a check, but it doesn't settle who owns and maintains it.

monday.blocker: Nobody in sales asked for it and nobody owns maintaining it. I also haven't checked the GDPR side for CRM data.

misconception.why: The attack arrives as ordinary text in a document, so the output can look fine while the agent has been steered. I'd still skip checking quality on routine tasks. For security I'd now run the check.

one_line: Good on 'give it less' and on sharing a skill without an owner. It's slow and repetitive for anyone already running agents.
